title: Redis MCP Server
summary: Let your agent read and write Redis strings, hashes, streams and vector indexes through the official Redis MCP server, run with uvx.
description: The Redis MCP server from Redis itself gives an agent typed tools for strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, JSON documents, pub/sub and streams, plus vector search through the query engine.

It runs locally over stdio with uvx and connects with the usual REDIS_ variables. The server has no read-only switch, so the safe route is a Redis ACL user that can only read, passed in as the username and password.
useWhen: Inspect what a cache key actually holds while debugging
Look at a stream and its consumer groups
Check TTLs on session keys before changing expiry
Try a vector index query against sample data

mcp.name: redis

env.name: REDIS_HOST
env.description: Hostname of the Redis server, default 127.0.0.1

env.name: REDIS_USERNAME
env.description: Redis ACL user, use a read-only one for safety

access: Reads and writes keys in the Redis database it connects to
Can publish to channels and add or delete stream entries unless the ACL user forbids it

example.prompt: List the keys that start with session: and tell me which ones have no expiry set.
example.result: Found 48 session: keys. 3 have no TTL (session:legacy-12, session:legacy-40, session:admin-tmp); the other 45 expire within 24 hours.

faq.question: Is there a read-only mode?
faq.answer: Not as a flag. Create an ACL user with read commands only, for example +@read -@write, and give its name and password to the server.

faq.question: Do I need Node?
faq.answer: No. Install uv instead: the server is distributed on PyPI and launched by uvx.

faq.question: Can it reach a hosted Redis with TLS?
faq.answer: Yes. The server documents a REDIS_SSL variable and certificate path variables for TLS connections.

access: Runs a local process that connects to the Redis instance you point it at
Writes allowed unless the Redis user is limited
